account: The knowledge state has 9 open questions and 0 answers; nothing can be synthesized or experimented on yet. The binding constraint on every downstream demand (mechanism, causal model, predictions, experiment) is knowing exactly what the seven papers found, under what conditions, and with what page markers. The highest-information next action is therefore a parallel extraction wave over the corpus. The three core debate papers (Du 2023 positive, Smit 2023 critical/null, Zhang 2025 reappraisal) are the conflicting empirical heart and each merits a dedicated investigation; the two social-influence papers (Lorenz 2011, Choi 2025) each ground the diversity/conformity pathway; Dung 1995 and Shapiro 2011 are formal scaffolding for synthesis/adjudication and are combined into one investigation to fit the six-investigation limit. All six read disjoint files and can complete without peer results.

investigations.acceptance_condition: An answer listing: tasks used; baselines compared; direction and approximate magnitude of debate's effect per task; scaling with agents/rounds; consensus/convergence observations; any stated failure modes or limitations; each item tagged with a PDF page marker from the file.
investigations.independence_account: Requires reading only du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt; no other investigation's output is needed.
investigations.question: What exactly does Du et al. 2023 (papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt) claim and show about multiagent debate: which tasks and baselines (single-agent, self-consistency/majority voting over independent samples), what were the quantitative effects, how do agents and rounds scale, what does the paper report about consensus/convergence and about cases where debate does not help, and what compute does the procedure consume relative to baselines? Record every key claim with its `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker.
investigations.rationale: This is the principal positive evidence that communication between agents helps; the note must represent it precisely, including its convergence-to-consensus dynamics and any compute asymmetry, before it can be reconciled with null results.

investigations.acceptance_condition: An answer listing: debate variants and tasks tested; baselines and whether compute was matched; tasks/metrics where debate did not help or hurt; the paper's own explanation of when debate helps; stated limitations; each with PDF page markers.
investigations.independence_account: Requires reading only smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt; independent of peer results.
investigations.question: What exactly does Smit et al. 2023 (papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt) find when re-examining multi-agent debate strategies: which debate variants and tasks were tested, which baselines (e.g., single-agent with equivalent sampling) were used, where did debate fail to beat or underperform simpler baselines, what role do model capability/size and judge aggregation play, and what matched-compute or cost comparisons does the paper make? Record key claims with `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
investigations.rationale: This is the principal null/adverse evidence against debate; its exact baselines and negative results define the conflict the note must reconcile rather than silently select between.

investigations.acceptance_condition: An answer listing: the proposed factor taxonomy; main empirical findings including at least two interactions or boundary conditions; stance toward prior positive MAD results; any compute/cost accounting; stated limitations; each with PDF page markers.
investigations.independence_account: Requires reading only zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt; independent of peer results.
investigations.question: What does Zhang et al. 2025 (papers/text/zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt, 'If Multi-Agent Debate Is the Answer, What Is the Question?') establish about the conditions under which multi-agent debate helps or fails: what taxonomy of factors (task type/difficulty, model heterogeneity, number of agents/rounds, topology, judge) is proposed, what are the headline empirical results and interactions, how does the paper position itself relative to Du et al. and other positive reports, and what does it say about compute costs? Record key claims with `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
investigations.rationale: This reappraisal paper likely contains the moderator structure (when MAD wins vs loses) that the note's causal model must absorb, extend, or contest; extracting its factor taxonomy and interactions is essential for the reconciliation demand.

investigations.acceptance_condition: An answer describing: experimental setup and conditions; the three signature effects (accuracy/diversity narrowing, confidence inflation, group convergence) with direction; which information conditions were better/worse; stated caveats; each with PDF page markers.
investigations.independence_account: Requires reading only lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt; independent of peer results.
investigations.question: What does Lorenz et al. 2011 (papers/text/lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt) show about how social influence affects the wisdom of crowds: the experimental design (tasks, rounds, information conditions), the measured effects of seeing others' estimates on individual accuracy, diversity of estimates, and confidence, the distinction between full information and aggregated-information conditions, and the quantitative pattern of when social influence helped vs undermined the crowd? Record key claims with `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
investigations.rationale: This is the foundational human evidence that exposure to others' answers can reduce collective accuracy by collapsing diversity while inflating confidence — the conformity pathway that any mechanism for agent communication must model and that predicts when an open transcript loses.

investigations.acceptance_condition: An answer describing: simulation design and scale; main conformity findings including majority and intelligence effects; any interaction between argument quality and group size; stated limitations; each with PDF page markers.
investigations.independence_account: Requires reading only choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt; independent of peer results.
investigations.question: What does Choi et al. 2025 (papers/text/choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt) show about conformity in LLM multi-agent debate: the simulation design (proponent/opponent/neutral agents, majority vs minority sizes, intelligence levels, topics), the main quantitative findings on majority effects and intelligence disparities, how persuasion quality vs quantity matters, and what this implies about when exposure to other agents' outputs shifts vs fails to shift an agent? Record key claims with `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
investigations.rationale: This is the LLM-side analogue of Lorenz: direct evidence on conformity dynamics inside LLM debates, including the finding that a single high-capability agent can outweigh a majority — a key fact for modeling who influences whom under different communication structures.

investigations.acceptance_condition: An answer giving: core definitions and guarantees from each paper; an explicit statement of what each framework abstracts away (truth, evidence quality, influence); and at least one observation per paper about a condition under which conflict-free merging or admissible-set reasoning preserves vs destroys information; with PDF page markers.
investigations.independence_account: Requires reading only the two named formal papers; independent of peer results.
investigations.question: What formal machinery do Dung 1995 (papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt) and Shapiro et al. 2011 (papers/text/shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt) provide that is relevant to agent communication design: for Dung, the definitions of argumentation frameworks, attack relations, admissible/preferred/stable/grounded extensions and what they guarantee about justified conclusions; for Shapiro, the definitions of CRDTs, strong eventual consistency, commutativity/idempotence and what they guarantee about merging concurrent updates without coordination. Note what each framework does NOT model (e.g., evidential weight, truth) since that limits their direct application. Record key definitions with `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
investigations.rationale: The note's synthesis/adjudication stage and its aggregation-only baseline need formal grounding: argumentation semantics can model structured Q/A conflict resolution, and CRDT results characterize when order-free aggregation loses nothing — together they bound what communication can add over merge-based aggregation.

action.wave_rationale: All six investigations are pure extractions from disjoint files with no cross-dependencies, so they can run in one frozen parallel wave; together they cover all seven corpus files and directly feed demands D4 and D3, setting up a later reconciliation/synthesis stage.
